articles.title: Maximizing Neurovascular Outcomes of Facial Transplantation: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.authors: Olivia A James, Faye Bennett
articles.abstract: Facial transplantation is a division of reconstructive surgery which aims to improve the function and appearance of a face that has endured severe disfigurement. Currently, the face transplant procedure uses allogenic tissue, harvested from a brain-dead donor, to replace damaged facial components. To date, 50 face transplants have been performed worldwide. Survival and functional success of the transplant is dependent on multiple factors; however, effective neurovascular recovery of the graft is arguably the most important. An effective vasculature system is essential to avoid necrosis and death of the transplanted tissue, and an effective nervous system is required for the graft to regain function. This comprehensive review examines and evaluates recommendations found in different studies to try and determine techniques for achieving optimal neurovascular graft outcomes. Sensory recovery of the graft occurs spontaneously through natural regeneration of the trigeminal nerve's cutaneous branches. Motor recovery, however, relies on precise coaptation of donor and recipient nerves using microsurgical sutures, reinforced by fibrin glue. Additional considerations, including parotid gland exclusion and use of a nerve graft, can further improve outcomes. Pre-operative vascular assessment of both the donor and recipient is another crucial consideration. Computed tomography angiography, magnetic resonance angiography, and digital subtraction angiography can be used to plan and enable successful end-to-end or end-to-side anastomosis of vessels. If applied in future facial transplantation procedures, these techniques could enhance recovery, improve functional outcomes, and lead to a greater patient quality of life.

articles.title: Early Ontogeny of Plesiopuntius bimaculatus (Bleeker, 1863): Embryonic Development and Comparative Perspectives Within Smiliogastrinae.
articles.authors: Melbin Lal, Dinesh M, Anvar Ali
articles.abstract: The present study provides the first comprehensive account of the embryonic and larval ontogeny of Plesiopuntius bimaculatus, a smiliogastrine cyprinid distributed in peninsular India and Sri Lanka, together with observations on its reproductive biology. Captive spawning produced small, adhesive, demersal eggs (696.46 ± 23.72 µm) deposited on vegetation and gravel, with no parental care observed. Embryogenesis followed the characteristic teleost developmental sequence, including meroblastic cleavage, epiboly-driven gastrulation, and sequential organogenesis, with hatching occurring approximately 16 h 15 min after fertilization at 27°C-28°C. Larvae hatched at 2.09 ± 0.08 mm total length and exhibited transient substrate adhesion, early swim bladder inflation, and the onset of exogenous feeding during the pre-flexion stage. Regression analyses revealed strong linear relationships among selected cranial and body measurements (R2 = 0.944-0.99), indicating coordinated changes in these dimensions during ontogeny. An ontogenetic shift from a terminal to a subterminal mouth position was also observed during juvenile development. Comparison with published developmental data for other smiliogastrine cyprinids revealed a broadly conserved developmental sequence, alongside differences in egg size, hatching size, and reported embryonic duration. These comparisons provide a basis for investigating potential differences in developmental timing among smiliogastrine taxa; however, heterochrony cannot be established from the available data because incubation conditions and developmental-stage criteria differ among studies. The findings expand knowledge of early development in P. bimaculatus and provide a foundation for further comparative research and captive-breeding applications.

articles.title: Age-related morphometric and morphological differences in the external aperture of the carotid canal: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Murat Inci, Hamza Kasar, Mehmet Selcuk et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate age-stratified morphometric estimates for the external aperture of the carotid canal (EACC) in a paediatric population; it also aimed to assess age-related differences in its morphological and morphometric characteristics and the relationship between its dimensions and transverse skull-base width, measured as the distance between the supramastoid crests (SC-to-SC). METHODS: This retrospective study included 700 EACCs obtained from 350 patients aged between 1 and 18 years, evenly distributed across five age groups. Length, width, estimated area of the EACC, and distances to the midline, supramastoid crest, and mandible were measured on computed tomography images. Morphological types were classified as round, oval, and distinctly transversely elongated according to the width-to-length ratio. Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) were used to account for bilateral shape dependency. RESULTS: The mean EACC length was 4.11 ± 0.88 mm, the width was 5.39 ± 1.19 mm and the estimated area was 18.03 ± 7.13 mm2. Age group had a very strong effect on all parameters (η2p = 0.389-0.822). Polynomial regression revealed an asynchronous trajectory: aperture dimensions peaked at 10-13 years (quadratic trend), whereas landmark distances increased linearly up to 14-18 years. After Bonferroni correction, EACC width, estimated area and SC-to-SC distance were significantly larger in males. Oval type predominated (56%), and the distinctly transversely elongated type was more common in males (GEE, p = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Growth of EACC parameters occurs asynchronously: canal dimensions reach maximum values in the 10-13-year age group, whereas distances to surrounding landmarks expand into late adolescence (14-18 years). These age-stratified estimates may assist anatomical orientation during preoperative radiological evaluation of the paediatric skull base.

articles.title: Postural control differences in children who are deaf or hard of hearing: A systematic review and meta-analysis of postural sway outcomes.
articles.authors: Hannah Ray, Maddie Gose, Nikolina Djumic et al.
articles.abstract: Children who are deaf and hard of hearing (DHH) may exhibit altered postural control due to differences in sensory inputs contributing to balance regulation. Quantitative synthesis of posturographic outcomes can clarify the magnitude and consistency of these differences while identifying methodological factors that limit comparability across studies. This review evaluated postural sway outcomes in DHH children relative to typically hearing peers. Following PRISMA guidelines, five databases were searched for studies employing static posturography in pediatric DHH populations. Twenty-five studies satisfied inclusion criteria for the systematic review and 12 studies were included in the meta-analysis. Standardized mean differences were calculated for anterior-posterior (AP) and medial-lateral (ML) sway metrics. Between-study heterogeneity was examined with attention to task conditions and measurement approaches. Pooled estimates indicated altered sway in DHH children, with AP and ML variability consistently differentiating groups. However, heterogeneity was high across tasks, and limited reporting of protocol features constrained evaluation of how postural difficulty, sensory conditions, and analysis choices influenced outcomes. Posturographic evidence supports meaningful differences in postural control between DHH and typically hearing children, but substantial heterogeneity of findings limits interpretability and cross-study comparison. Given the need for greater standardization in task design, outcome selection, and reporting to advance mechanistic understanding for pediatric balance assessment, we provide methodological recommendations for future investigations to inform the development of standardized assessment protocols.

articles.title: Proteomic Interrogation of the Acute Response to Muscle Damage in Untrained Middle Aged and Older Females.
articles.authors: J Max Michel, Sophia C Bamman, Franccesco P Boeno et al.
articles.abstract: Blunted regenerative responses to muscle damage with aging are linked to inflammatory signaling and satellite cell dynamics; however, most evidence is derived from males and is limited to targeted assays of bulk muscle tissue and/or circulating biomarkers. Here, we focused on middle-aged and older females and leveraged multi-compartment proteomics to identify responses to modest muscle damage across myofibrillar (MYOF), sarcoplasmic (SARCO), and serum compartments. Sixteen females (mean age = 61±8 years) had vastus lateralis biopsies and serum collected before (PRE) and 24 h after (POST) a resistance loading protocol that induced modest muscle damage (72.9% increase in serum creatine kinase activity). SARCO and MYOF fractions were separated using differential centrifugation, and proteomics was performed on three compartments using a nanoparticle capture approach followed by mass spectrometry, yielding 9,059 proteins in SARCO, 4,334 in MYOF, and 3,964 in serum. The protocol produced 90 differentially abundant (DA) proteins in SARCO (61 up, 29 down), 39 in MYOF (27 up, 12 down), and 124 in serum (34 up (9 muscle-specific), 90 down). DA proteins minimally overlapped across compartments. Enrichment analyses pointed primarily to translation-related processes in MYOF and contractile processes in serum. Pathway Level Information ExtractoR performed on all DA proteins identified multi-compartment biocircuits linked to membrane trafficking, vesicle mediated transport, neutrophil degranulation, and viral infection. Viral infection-related proteins correlated with body weight and body fat, while vesicle mediated transport-related proteins correlated with serum creatine kinase activity. This analysis reveals novel biocircuitry of modest muscle damage in middle-aged and older females.

articles.title: Functional sympatholysis: Do females do it better?
articles.authors: Gabriele Marinari, Breanne S Collison, Darren S DeLorey
articles.abstract: Our laboratory has recently shown that contraction-mediated inhibition of sympathetic vasoconstriction (sympatholysis) was enhanced in female compared with male rats. The purpose of this study was to investigate the hypothesis that sympatholysis would be enhanced in young females compared to young males during moderate (MOD)- and heavy (HVY)-intensity alternate-leg knee-extension (KE) exercise. Young (age 22±3), healthy adults (8 males, 8 females) performed a cold pressor test (CPT) at rest and during MOD- (30% of peak work rate) and HVY- (60% of peak work rate) intensity KE exercise. Blood pressure was measured via Finometer and mean arterial pressure (MAP) was calculated. Femoral blood flow (FBF) was measured using Doppler ultrasound, and femoral vascular conductance (FVC) was calculated as FVC=FBF·MAP-1. Sympathetic vasoconstrictor responsiveness was defined as the percent decrease in FVC (%ΔFVC) in response to the CPT. Sympatholysis was defined as the difference between the %ΔFVC response to the CPT at rest and during exercise. Sympathetic vasoconstrictor responsiveness was not different (p>0.05) between males (-40.5±8.8%) and females (-46.0±10.4%) at rest. During exercise, sympathetic vasoconstrictor responsiveness was blunted in an exercise intensity-dependent manner in both males and females (p<0.001). However, sympatholysis was greater in females than in males during both MOD- (male: 13.2±6.2%; female: 26.7±9.0%; p<0.01) and HVY- (male: 25.3±7.3%; female: 36.1±8.0%; p<0.01) intensity exercise. Consistent with our previous findings in rats, sympatholysis was enhanced in human young females compared with males. These data provide further evidence that biological sex modulates sympathetic vascular control in the skeletal muscle vascular bed during exercise.

articles.title: Mechanisms Influencing Maximum Joint Range of Motion and Stiffness: A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Camila D Lima, Anthony J Blazevich
articles.abstract: Joint 'flexibility' is an encompassing term influenced by both a joint's maximum range of motion (ROMmax) and its resistance to rotation, i.e. its stiffness. A critical amount of flexibility is thought to be important for both sports performance and daily and occupational tasks. Improvements in joint ROMmax, specifically, are often assumed to result from material and mechanical changes in the joint's soft tissue structures; however, they also may result from changes in sensory information relayed from peripheral receptors to the brain, or the interpretation of that information. Changes in psychological state mediated by pain, state arousal and other psychological factors can therefore influence the voluntary capacity of individuals to tolerate a stretch, and thus their ROMmax. Stiffness, on the other hand, may be affected by both muscular and non-muscular tissues, although the most important sources of stiffness are yet to be agreed upon. In this narrative review, we define important terms as well as the factors impacting stiffness and ROMmax. We assert that joint stiffness is affected by the extracellular matrix, intramuscular fat and water as well as fascicle rotation, and that these factors also by extension may affect ROMmax. While sarcomere (and fibre) stiffness is largely regulated by the giant protein titin, it plays a lesser role at the whole muscle level. Alternatively, ROMmax can be influenced by our processing of sensory information and the decisions we make (consciously or subconsciously) about our willingness to stretch further. Thus, cognitive and attention processes can influence an individual's decision to stop a stretch.

articles.title: The Global Physical Literacy Action Framework: Process and Outcomes.
articles.authors: Johannes Carl, Lisa M Barnett, Alethea Jerebine et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Physical literacy integrates physical, affective, cognitive and social elements into a holistic framework for physical activity. Despite the increasing recognition of physical literacy across many sectors, the entire field lacks a prospective roadmap for research, practice and policy. OBJECTIVE: Seeking to determine the content of a 'Global Physical Literacy (GloPL) Action Framework,' this study aimed to define goals, principles, actions and pathways that can advance the physical literacy field worldwide. METHODS: A group Delphi study (based on published protocol) engaged 59 physical literacy-focused academics from 46 countries, 7 representatives of literature gaps, and 24 individuals representing societies/organisations. The representatives independently generated ideas for action through online surveys (Qualtrics). The ideas underwent reflexive thematic analysis (NVivo), informing the subsequent discussions in six online meetings. All decisions were supported by formal voting with pre-defined agreement thresholds for two rounds of voting. RESULTS: Analysis resulted in 849 initial codes grouped into five themes: advocacy, practice, education, assessment and research. Members discussed 15 central topics, of which six reached agreement in the first voting round and nine in the second voting round. Key recommendations included: establishing a core set of physical literacy elements/principles (advocacy); generating more resources/programmes on physical literacy (practice); aligning physical education curricula with physical literacy principles (education); assessing physical literacy at the population level (assessment); and emphasising implementation science (research). CONCLUSIONS: The comprehensive consensus findings will inform the pillars of the first GloPL Action Framework. Its release marks the beginning of a dynamic process intended to guide coordinated actions on physical literacy in education, public health, sport, healthcare/promotion, rehabilitation, active recreation and community services/development.

articles.title: Distinct neural input strategies to motor units in the soleus and medial gastrocnemius during quiet standing.
articles.authors: Hiroki Arakawa, Naotsugu Kaneko, Nadaka Hakariya et al.
articles.abstract: Standing posture control depends on the soleus (SOL) and medial gastrocnemius (MG), which serve distinct functional roles. Identifying neural mechanisms remains challenging because invasive techniques sample few motor units (MUs). High-density surface electromyography (HDsEMG) enables MU analysis and estimation of common inputs to motoneurons. Leveraging this approach, and by comparing standing with an isometric voluntary contraction performed at an EMG level matched to standing, we aimed to elucidate standing-specific common synaptic inputs underlying the distinct MU behaviors of the SOL and MG. We recorded HDsEMG and electroencephalographic signals from 20 males during standing and isometric contractions. EMG signals were decomposed into MU activity, with common inputs estimated through intramuscular and corticomuscular coherence (IMC and CMC). IMC was used as an index of common inputs to motoneurons, whereas CMC was used as an index of corticomuscular connectivity. During standing, the MG exhibited higher alpha- and beta-band IMC than the SOL. Compared with isometric contraction, CMC decreased during standing in the delta-, alpha- nd beta-bands in both muscles, whereas beta-band IMC remained unchanged only in the MG. These findings suggest that MG motoneurons receive more common synaptic input during standing than SOL motoneurons. Although CMC decreased similarly in both muscles, MG maintained higher IMC, suggesting a relatively greater role of non-cortical common input in the MG. This pattern could reflect differences in the functional roles of the MG and SOL in postural control, with MG contributing to force adjustments that counteract body sway and SOL contributing to stable tonic force production. KEY POINTS: Using high-density surface electromyography, we examined motor unit activity and neural inputs to medial gastrocnemius and soleus during standing. The medial gastrocnemius shows greater common synaptic input than the soleus, potentially associated with its role in phasic ankle plantarflexion torque generation to correct postural sway. The soleus exhibits lower motor unit synchrony, potentially associated with its role in generating stable and continuous ankle plantarflexion torque for body weight support. Corticomuscular coherence was lower during standing than during isometric voluntary contraction in both muscles, suggesting that functional corticomuscular coupling was similarly reduced in the medial gastrocnemius and soleus during standing. This study suggests differences in common synaptic input to soleus and medial gastrocnemius motoneurons, potentially associated with their distinct functional roles during standing.

articles.title: Adenosine-driven P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase and protein kinase A signalling constrains 5HT2a receptor-induced phrenic motor facilitation.
articles.authors: Kayla A Burrowes, Gordon S Mitchell
articles.abstract: Episodic activation of spinal serotonin receptors elicits phrenic motor facilitation (pMF), a form of respiratory motor plasticity. Although 5-HT2 and 5-HT7 receptors elicit pMF, they do so via distinct cellular mechanisms known as the Q (5-HT2A/B) and S (5-HT7) pathways. These pathways interact via mutual crosstalk inhibition; thus, concurrent activation of both serotonin receptor subtypes diminishes/abolishes pMF. Although episodic spinal adenosine 2A (A2a) receptor activation also elicits pMF via the S pathway, it remains unclear whether 5-HT2 and A2a receptors interact via similar mechanisms. Although some molecules mediating crosstalk inhibition between 5-HT2 and 5-HT7 receptors have been identified, little is known concerning 5-HT2 and A2a receptor interactions. Thus, we tested the hypotheses that: (1) concurrent 5-HT2 and A2a receptor activation diminishes pMF via mutual crosstalk inhibition, and (2) A2a receptors inhibit 5-HT2a-induced pMF via mechanisms that require p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and/or protein kinase A (PKA) enzymatic activity. Selective 5-HT2a and A2a receptor agonists were delivered intrathecally at C4 (3, 6 µL injections, 5 min intervals) in urethane-anaesthetized, ventilated, vagotomized and paralysed Sprague Dawley rats. Spinal 5-HT2a (73 ± 12%) or A2a (90 ± 17%) receptor activation increased integrated phrenic burst amplitude (i.e. pMF). Concurrent receptor activation abolished pMF (15 ± 7.7%), demonstrating crosstalk inhibition. Spinal p38 MAP kinase or protein kinase A inhibition restored pMF, implicating both kinases as key mediators of crosstalk inhibition. Although the functional significance of these complex interactions is not yet fully understood, greater mechanistic understanding will accelerate progress towards optimizing the therapeutic efficacy of acute intermittent hypoxia-induced respiratory motor plasticity. KEY POINTS: Concurrent 5-HT2a (Q pathway) and A2a (S pathway) receptor activation cancels phrenic motor facilitation via mutual crosstalk inhibition. Spinal p38 MAPK or protein kinase A inhibition restores phrenic motor facilitation with concurrent Q and S pathway activation, demonstrating a key role for these kinases in crosstalk inhibition.

articles.title: Exploring the role of brain-derived neurotrophic factor as a biomarker in female infertility: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Ariane M Zanesco, Natália S Tonet, Maisa M Araújo et al.
articles.abstract: Bain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is essential for neuronal survival and development, and is also involved in oogenesis, follicle recruitment, and germ cell survival, which could impact reproduction. However, in humans, the relationship between BDNF levels and infertility remains controversial. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to explore the available evidence on the variation of BDNF levels in the body fluids of women and men and their interface with different conditions that could affect reproductive functions. Data were independently extracted by two reviewers. A systematic search was performed on six databases. Of the 1,735 studies identified, 20 were included in the qualitative synthesis and 15 in the meta-analysis. Meta-analysis was performed for all studies regarding infertility markers, and then, specifically, only for studies that evaluated endometriosis and other cases of infertility. Of the 20 studies included in the systematic review, only one evaluated sperm dysfunction in men. Of the 19 studies conducted in women, 13 evaluated endometriosis, 4 evaluated amenorrhea, 1 evaluated premature ovarian failure, and 1 evaluated different outcomes on childbirth. In the meta-analysis, BDNF levels were associated with endometriosis and other conditions that lead to infertility. Our findings confirm that BDNF levels are dysregulated in infertility conditions. However, the analyses showed substantial heterogeneity and, in some cases, evidence of publication bias. Further studies evaluating infertility in men and that include body mass index (BMI), estrogen levels, and the menstrual cycle phase at the time of collection in women are crucial for obtaining more robust results.

articles.title: Countermovement Jump Performance Across Ten Competitive Microcycles in Under-18 Soccer Players: An Analysis of Delayed and Long-Term Responses to Training and Official Competition.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Rodrigo Villaseca-Vicuña, Tomás T Freitas, Konstantinos Spyrou et al.
articles.abstract: Villaseca-Vicuña, R, Freitas, TT, Spyrou, K, Marín-Cascales, E, Comyns, T, Loturco, I, and Zabaloy, S. Countermovement jump performance across 10 competitive microcycles in under-18 soccer players: An analysis of delayed and long-term responses to training and official competition. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aims of this study were to (a) determine within-microcycle changes in countermovement jump (CMJ) measures (i.e., jump height, reactive strength index modified [RSImod], and eccentric peak velocity [EPV]) collected 2 days after (MD+2) and 1 day before (MD-1) the match-day across 10 weeks during the competitive period in under-18 soccer players and (b) analyze week-to-week variations in the selected CMJ-metrics collected on MD+2 across the entire mesocycle. Twelve (n = 12) under-18 academy soccer players (age: 17.5 ± 0.5 years; body mass: 71.9 ± 7.7 kg) volunteered to participate in this study. Over 10 competitive weeks, CMJ assessments were recorded on force plates at 2 key microcycle time points: MD+2 (active recovery phase at the start of the microcycle) and MD-1 (end of the microcycle). Results showed significant within-week changes in CMJ height and EPV in most of the training microcycles (p: <0.001 to 0.049) while RSImod showed significant changes in only 4 of the 10 microcycles (p: 0.001 to 0.049). Similarly, the between-week comparisons showed significant variations only in EPV and RSI (p: 0.005 to 0.049). These findings suggest that jump height might be better suited to assess within-week changes, while RSImod appears to hold greater discriminative value for detecting between-week fluctuations. Eccentric peak velocity, in turn, may provide useful information for both within-week and between-week changes in young soccer players.

articles.title: Architectural and Force-Producing Characteristics of Knee Extensor Muscles Between Alpine Skiers and Road Cyclists.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Tae-Gyu Han, Hae-Dong Lee
articles.abstract: Han, T-G and Lee, H-D. Architectural and force-producing characteristics of knee extensor muscles between alpine skiers and road cyclists. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study aimed to investigate whether muscle architecture and torque characteristics differ among athletes subjected to different sport-specific loading conditions. Alpine skiers (AS; n = 9, predominantly eccentric [ECC]-loading exposure) and road cyclists (RC; n = 9, predominantly concentric [CON]-loading exposure) were recruited. Muscle architecture (fascicle length, pennation angle, and thickness) of the vastus lateralis (VL) was measured at rest using ultrasonography at 10° and 100° of knee flexion. Maximum voluntary isometric (ISO) knee-extension torque was measured at 40°, 60°, 80°, and 100° of knee flexion, from which the optimum joint angle and peak ISO torque were estimated. Peak knee-extension torque was measured during CON and ECC contractions over a knee-flexion range of 0°-110° at 30°/s and 150°/s. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Among the architectural variables, RC exhibited greater VL thickness than AS at 10° of knee flexion, whereas fascicle length and pennation angle did not differ between groups. Compared with RC, AS showed significantly greater ISO knee-extension torque at 100° (p < 0.05). The estimated optimum joint angle was also greater in AS (p < 0.05). Absolute ECC peak torque did not differ significantly between groups; however, AS demonstrated greater ECC torque when values were normalized to the estimated peak ISO torque. These findings show that AS and RC demonstrate different knee-extensor torque-angle and torque-velocity characteristics despite similar VL fascicle length and pennation angle. They further indicate that knee-extensor force-producing characteristics may be shaped by the dominant loading and contraction-mode demands repeatedly experienced in each sport.

articles.title: Performance and Physiological Responses to Strength Training Programs in Elite Judo Athletes.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Bruno T Campos, João Gabriel D S Rodrigues, Cesar C Cal Abad et al.
articles.abstract: Campos, BT, Rodrigues, JGdS, Cal Abad, CC, Bachi, ALL, dos Santos, CMM, Tritto, AC, Kons, RL, Penna, EM, and Prado, LS. Performance and physiological responses to strength training programs in elite judo athletes. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study compared the effects of 2 short-term strength training models, block planning (BP) and undulating planning (UP), on performance, physiological, and perceptual responses in elite judo athletes. We hypothesized that BP would induce greater physiological strain due to the concentration of training stimuli. Eighteen judokas (14 men and 4 women) were randomly assigned to BP (n = 9) or UP (n = 9) for 4 weeks, performing 6 weekly strength sessions alongside technical-tactical training. Performance outcomes included countermovement jump (CMJ), muscle power (back squat and bent-over row), and the Special Judo Fitness Test (SJFT). Monitoring variables included internal load, heart rate variability (HRV), and well-being, while physiological markers included creatine kinase, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and cortisol. Data were analyzed using 2-way repeated-measures ANOVA (p < 0.05). Both groups improved SJFT performance (p < 0.01), with no between-group differences. Block planning increased lower-limb peak power (p = 0.01; d = 0.90), whereas UP showed no meaningful change. Upper-limb power and CMJ did not change in either group. Internal load showed different temporal patterns between models. Block planning presented higher HRVcv values (p = 0.04), indicating greater autonomic perturbation. Creatine kinase and TNF-α increased over time in both groups (p ≤ 0.05), while cortisol showed an interaction without clear post hoc differences. In conclusion, BP improved lower-limb power but increased physiological strain, whereas UP elicited similar judo-specific improvements with lower recovery demands. These findings highlight the importance of training organization for balancing performance and recovery in elite judo athletes.

articles.title: Effect of Repeat Deceleration on Countermovement Jump and Kicking Performance in Male and Female Football Players.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Xiaobin Wei, Huanhuan Zhu, Xuefeng Zheng et al.
articles.abstract: Wei, X, Zhu, H, Zheng, X, Gao, Y, Huang, J, Chen, X, Vigh-Larsen, JF, Mohr, M, and Krustrup, P. Greater reductions in deceleration compared with sprint ability following repeated high-intensity exercise in male and female soccer players, but no effect on countermovement jump (CMJ) or ball-kicking performance. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to examine the acute effect of repeated sprint and deceleration on the fatigue of each component (sprint vs. deceleration) and on CMJ and soccer kicking performance, and to investigate the association between deceleration ability and fatigue. Thirty-three high-level male (n = 18) and female (n = 15) college soccer players completed 10 × 15-m sprints with subsequent 5-m enforced deceleration, interspersed with 20-s recovery intervals. Sprint and deceleration performance were measured continuously during the protocol, while CMJ and kicking performance were assessed before and immediately after. Furthermore, the players' deceleration ability was measured using deceleration deficit and deceleration index. Peak deceleration had significantly higher fatigue index (FI) and decrement score (Sdec) compared with speed (p < 0.05, Cohen's d = 3.18-3.32), while no significant decline was found in CMJ or kicking performance after the repeated sprint and deceleration protocol (p > 0.05, Cohen's d = -0.06∼0.23). A significant repeated sprint and deceleration × sex interaction effect was observed in peak ball speed (p < 0.05, ηp2 = 0.149), with women showing a decrease in peak ball speed compared with their male counterparts. The deceleration index correlated with FI and Sdec of speed (r = -0.444∼-0.516, p < 0.05), and the rate of CMJ decline correlated with FI and Sdec deceleration (r = 0.530-0.549, p < 0.05). Finally, the rate of decline in kicking speed was positively correlated with the Sdec deceleration rate (r = 0.423, p < 0.05). Deceleration capacity is more prone to acute fatigue than sprint ability. In addition, repeated sprint and deceleration had a limited effect on athletic performance, but men and women showed different adjusted trends in kicking speed. Finally, players having better deceleration capacity show a smaller performance drop.

articles.title: Saturated and Trans Fatty Acids Were Not Associated with All-Cause or Cause-Specific Mortality in a Japanese Population with Relatively Low Intakes: The Japan Public Health Center-Based Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Kumiko Kito, Junko Ishihara, Ayaka Kotemori et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines recommend that saturated fatty acids (SFAs) and trans fatty acids (TFAs) should comprise ≤10% and ≤1% of total energy intake, respectively. However, evidence of the mortality risk associated with increased TFA and SFA intake in populations with a relatively low fat intake is limited. OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between total fat, SFA, TFA, monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA), and polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) intake and all-cause and cause-specific mortality in a Japanese population. METHODS: We included 90,807 participants aged 45-74 years with no history of cancer or cardiovascular disease (CVD). Dietary assessment was performed using a validated food frequency questionnaire. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models for each quintile of dietary fat intake: total fat, SFA, MUFA, PUFA, TFA, industrially-derived TFA (i-TFAs), and ruminant-derived TFA (r-TFA). RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 18.9 years, 22,618 deaths occurred. None of the analyses of fat intakes in quintiles showed a positive association with all-cause mortality for higher intakes of all fats, even for i-TF. In females, a nominally significant association was observed for all-cause mortality with PUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.92 [0.84-0.997]) and cancer mortality with MUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.84 [0.73-0.97]).In females, higher intakes of total fat and MUFA were nominally associated with higher respiratory disease mortality, whereas a higher SFA intake showed a suggestive association (P for trend <0.05). CONCLUSIONS: In this study, neither SFA nor TFA intake was positively associated with all-cause mortality, and higher PUFA intake was inversely associated with all-cause mortality in females.

articles.title: Eicosapentaenoic acid in adipose tissue is associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke: A Danish case-cohort study.
articles.authors: Johanne Havskov Thygesen, Villads Bové Hesislev, Phillip Czerwonka et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have been linked to a lower risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, however, their association with hemorrhagic stroke remains uncertain. We investigated associations between adipose tissue content of individual omega-3 PUFAs (α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosapentaenoic acid (DPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), the sum of EPA+DHA), and the risk of hemorrhagic stroke and its subtypes intracranial and subarachnoid hemorrhage. METHODS: This case-cohort study based on the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health Cohort included 54,546 men and women aged 50 to 65 years at baseline (1993-1997). Adipose tissue composition of omega-3 PUFAs was determined by gas chromatography for all hemorrhagic stroke cases and within a randomly drawn subcohort of 4,615 participants. Cases were identified by linkage to the Danish National Patient Register. Hazard ratios (HR) were obtained by weighted Cox regression. RESULTS: During a median of 21 years follow-up, we identified 729 hemorrhagic stroke cases. In multivariable analyses, a significant inverse association between the content of EPA in adipose tissue and the risk of total hemorrhagic stroke was found. Thus, the HR for hemorrhagic stroke was 0.64 (95% CI: 0.50-0.82) when comparing the highest quintile of EPA content in adipose tissue with the lowest. Associations were similar when stratified according to sex and when investigating subtypes of hemorrhagic stroke, although findings were not statistically significant for subarachnoid hemorrhages. No statistically significant associations were observed between adipose tissue content of DHA, DPA and EPA+DHA and hemorrhagic strokes. A high content of ALA in adipose tissue was associated with a higher risk of hemorrhagic stroke (HR for quintile 5 vs. 1: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.01-1.72). CONCLUSION: A high content of EPA in adipose tissue was associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke, while a high content of ALA was associated with a higher risk in this cohort.

articles.title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.authors: Mohamed Achraf Harrabi, Thouraya Fendri, Rahma Ayed et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA. METHODS: This randomized controlled trial enrolled young women with IDA aged 18-25 years, who were randomly assigned to a training group (TG; n = 16) or a non-training group (NTG; n = 17). All participants received oral iron supplementation (ferrous sulfate, 494.5 mg/day, administered as 247.25 mg twice daily), while the TG additionally completed an 8-week extremely low-volume HIIT program based on plyometric exercises. Hemoglobin (Hb) and serum ferritin concentrations were assessed, alongside muscle endurance, reaction time performance, and postural control. Muscle endurance was evaluated using the Killy test, reaction time performance using an online simple reaction time test, and postural control using a stabilometric platform under bipodal and semi-tandem stance conditions. Postural assessments were conducted with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) on firm and foam surfaces. All outcomes were measured at baseline and 72 h after the final intervention session. RESULTS: After the 8-week intervention, this study demonstrated significant improvements across both groups, irrespective of the intervention. However, TG showed significantly greater post-intervention improvements than NTG in Hb concentration (P = 0.042), muscle endurance (P < 0.001), and postural control. Superior postural control in TG was observed during a bipedal stance on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.001); EC: P = 0.035), as well as during semi-tandem stance on a firm surface (EO: P = 0.015; EC: P = 0.040) and on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.019; EC: P = 0.003), compared to the NTG. With a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold for multiple comparisons (α = 0.00625), between-group differences in postural control remained significant for bipedal foam EO (P = 0.001) and semi-tandem foam EC (P = 0.003). CONCLUSIONS: The study showed that women with IDA improved their postural performance regardless of the intervention used. However, an 8-week program of extremely low-volume HIIT combined with plyometric exercises and iron supplementation had a more beneficial effect compared to traditional iron therapy. These greater improvements in postural control occurred alongside greater improvements in the Hb concentration and muscle endurance in the TG compared to the NTG.

articles.title: Effects of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on physical function and body composition in older adults: a narrative review.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.authors: Rachel H Barclay, Marlena C Kruger, Matthew J Barnes
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Healthy aging is a priority for many individuals; however, a decline in physical function and poor body composition are common age-related changes that can cause the added years from rising life expectancy to be spent in poor health. Consequently, understanding the mechanisms involved in aging has become increasingly important, including the role of phospholipids (PLs) and how age-related changes in PL content may interfere with lipid metabolism and normal functioning of the musculoskeletal system. Milk fat globule membrane (MFGM) is a bovine milk fraction rich in PLs that may have the potential to support good physical health, so that quality of life can rise alongside life expectancy. METHODS: This narrative review was based on a literature search conducted on Google Scholar, PubMed, and Scopus in May 2026 using the following keywords and Boolean operators: milk fat globule membrane OR MFGM AND physical function OR body composition OR older adults. Studies were included if they were randomized clinical trials (RCTs) investigating MFGM's effects on physical function and/or body composition in older adults. RESULTS: Findings suggest that MFGM supplementation, when consumed in conjunction with exercise, is an effective way to improve physical function in older adults, particularly among Japanese cohorts; however, changes in habitual diet in response to exercise, variable PL concentrations, and other added ingredients used in interventions may have influenced these results. In contrast, its effects on body composition appear more modest, with some studies reporting no benefits, especially when exercise was not part of the study design, or when compliance may have been a factor. CONCLUSIONS: Beyond the combined use of supplementation and exercise, future RCTs should consistently report participant compliance and, where possible, examine MFGM as a standalone intervention to distinguish its effects from other bioactive ingredients. Greater standardization is also needed, particularly regarding PL dose. Studies should also aim to include participants from more diverse ethnic backgrounds to capture a wider range of physiological responses and improve generalizability of the findings.

articles.title: Dietary fibre intake and suicide in Japanese adults: the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Akiko Nanri, Tetsuya Mizoue, Atsushi Goto et al.
articles.abstract: Dietary fibre intake has been reported to be inversely associated with depression in a meta-analysis. However, most studies were cross-sectional, and none examined the association with suicide, a severe outcome of depression. We investigated the association of dietary fibre intake with suicide risk among Japanese adults. Participants were 40 630 men and 48 178 women aged 44-76 years who responded to the second survey (baseline of the present study) of the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study (1995-1998). Dietary fibre intake was assessed using a validated FFQ. Hazard ratios of suicide through December 2018 were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression analysis. During a mean follow-up of 18·7 years, we identified 459 deaths from suicide. Dietary fibre intake was associated with lower suicide risk after adjustment for covariates, including intakes of vitamin B12, vitamin D, Ca, Zn and n-3 PUFA. The multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio for suicide of the highest v. lowest quartile of total dietary fibre intake was 0·65 (95 % CI 0·46-0·93). Similar inverse associations were observed for vegetable and fruit fibre intake but not cereal or bean fibre. However, these associations were substantially attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for nutrients highly correlated with dietary fibre intake, including folate, vitamin B6, Mg and Fe; the corresponding value for total dietary fibre intake was 0·85 (95 % CI 0·55-1·31). Our findings suggest that greater consumption of foods rich in dietary fibre and related nutrients, rather than dietary fibre per se, may play a protective role against suicide.

articles.title: Mediterranean Diet Adherence and Markers of Healthy Aging: A Systematic Review of Biological and Functional Outcomes.
articles.authors: Mirko Marino, Cristian Del Bo', Martina Frigerio et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Aging involves molecular, cellular, and functional changes that increase vulnerability to chronic disease, cognitive decline, frailty, and loss of independence. Mediterranean-style dietary patterns are generally rich in plant foods, unsaturated fats, fiber, and bioactive compounds, but their composition varies across studies and may include modified or multicomponent interventions. OBJECTIVE: This Systematic Review evaluated associations between Mediterranean-style dietary adherence and related interventions and markers of healthy aging, including biological aging biomarkers, cognition, frailty, physical performance, and overall health status. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published during 2013- 2025. Searches were conducted in April 2025 and updated in August 2025. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251107773). DATA EXTRACTION: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies in adults were eligible if they assessed Mediterranean-style dietary patterns or interventions and reported aging-related biomarkers or functional outcomes. Two reviewers independently conducted study selection and data extraction. DATA ANALYSIS: Eleven studies were included: 5 RCTs, 4 prospective cohort studies, and 2 cross-sectional studies. Greater adherence was associated with better cognitive performance and slower memory decline in some studies. Favorable findings were also reported for telomere dynamics, epigenetic age, and inflammatory biomarkers. Improvements in frailty and physical performance were mainly observed in interventions combining dietary modification with physical activity. Heterogeneity in dietary definitions, adherence measures, intervention components, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis. CONCLUSIONS: The evidence suggests that favorable associations exist between Mediterranean-style dietary patterns and selected markers of healthy aging but does not establish uniform or causal effects. Interpretation is limited by methodological heterogeneity, self-reported dietary exposure, and the inclusion of modified or multicomponent interventions. Long-term studies using standardized dietary definitions, harmonized outcomes, objective adherence measures, and designs capable of isolating diet-specific effects are needed. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. [https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251107773].
